long_biography.plain_text:
Harold Lang Jewelers built an interstate trade by taking jewellery directly to stores. From about 1970, the Florida company regularly sold and consigned merchandise in North Carolina, with representatives delivering pieces, collecting returns and finalising transactions during repeated visits. The route endured for more than three decades and made personal, recurring contact central to the business model.

Harold Theodore Lang served as the company's president, overseeing a Miami-based operation while living in Naples. Decades later, another namesake venture, Harold Lang Jewelry LLC, placed him in management and continued the same commercial identity. Although both entities are now inactive and little is known publicly about his early life, his sustained career in jewellery distribution and retail supply remains clear.
